subject: Sentinel: tiered velocity hurdles and micro‑tranche offer
messages:

Subject: Intro + high level volume shape and ask

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. We ran the projection with product and expect roughly 25B total tokens in year one if we ramp as planned, with a big velocity spike during Q4 launches. Quick ask: does Redwood prefer a marginal ladder (rate applies only to tokens in each tranche) or a blended effective rate (single effective $/k based on committed volume)? Our procurement team also wants a sample invoice math (monthly) so they can reconcile to budget.

I attached a simple monthly profile (sentinel_volume_profile.csv) — it’s a projection not a firm commitment. Major constraints: quarterly invoicing, SOC2 evidence required, and a preference for a one‑year term.

Can you send a short proposal we can show procurement?

— Ara

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ara Gupta <ara@sentinel.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-06-11T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: SNT proposal — marginal vs blended worked examples and micro‑tranches

Ara / Marissa — attaching a compact proposal (SNT-proposal-20290611.pdf) with two worked examples and invoice mockups. Notes / highlights:

1) Offer shapes we modeled (monthly tokens and effective $/1K tokens):
   - Marginal ladder (per 1k tokens):
     * 0–750M / month: $2.40 per 1K
     * 750M–2.1B / month: $1.90 per 1K
     * 2.1B+ / month: $1.40 per 1K
   - Blended target: single effective rate if you commit 2.1B/mo = $1.95 per 1K (monthly true‑up, billed quarterly)

2) Micro‑tranches: we introduced 250M micro‑tranches for quarter‑to‑quarter ramp smoothing so that short spikes only partially move you into the next tier (reduces clawback surprises). That’s described in section 3 of the PDF.

3) Velocity credits: for customers who demonstrate >20% month‑over‑month growth in a 3‑month window we can apply a temporary velocity credit (30 days) instead of immediately moving to the higher marginal tier — helps during product launches.

4) Procurement/invoice view: last page shows an example invoice for May with a monthly true‑up and quarterly prepay reconciliation.

Tradeoffs short: marginal ladders reward growth but produce non‑linear invoice swings; blended simplifies forecasting for your finance team. Micro‑tranches + velocity credits are a middle ground.

If you want, we can convert the PDF to a one‑page comparison tailored to procurement language.

— Karthik
Director, Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
From: Ara Gupta <ara@sentinel.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sentinel.ai
Date: 2029-06-12T10:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SNT proposal — marginal vs blended worked examples and micro‑tranches

Thanks Karthik — useful framing and the micro‑tranche idea is interesting. Procurement reviewed the invoice mock and had two asks:

1) They want a single blended effective rate in the contract for budgeting. Procurement will accept a quarterly true‑up, but invoice volatility month‑to‑month is a non‑starter.
2) They’re asking if Redwood will accept a 2.1B tokens/month committed floor (12‑month) in exchange for a blended effective target of $1.80 per 1K tokens — with standard termination/true‑up clauses.

Also request: please attach SOC2 evidence and standard terms (our legal prefers to see a redline).

Can you come back with a redlineable term sheet?

— Ara
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-06-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: internal: negotiation posture for SNT counter

Marissa / Karthik — quick internal note on the counter:

- Procurement asking $1.80 / 1K on a blended 2.1B/mo commitment is aggressive relative to our cost curve, but we have levers: term length (12 vs 24), invoicing cadence (quarterly prepay required), and velocity credit ceilings.
- Suggested concession ladder:
  * Offer blended $1.95 / 1K if they sign 12 months and agree to quarterly prepay with 30‑day ramp protection.
  * If they insist on $1.80, require 18‑month term + 25% upfront or a minimum annual spend guarantee that reduces finance risk.
  * Keep micro‑tranche smoothing in the agreement to avoid month‑to‑month sticker shock.
- Need SOC2 and a security contact in the contract appendix; security will provide SOC2 report (not public copy) and put a 30‑day SLA for evidence requests.

If you want, I’ll draft the term sheet language and a short finance memo showing effective margin at $1.95 vs $1.80.

— Logan
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ara Gupta <ara@sentinel.ai>, procurement@sentinel.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-06-14T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood counterproposal — Sentinel commitment and terms

Ara / Procurement — thanks for the candid ask and the timeline. Attached are the term sheet and SOC2 evidence (redwood-terms-sentinel.pdf, SOC2-report-2028.pdf) and a DocuSign link for convenience. Summary of our counter: 

- Commitment: 2.1B tokens / month (12‑month term) with quarterly true‑up and reconciliation.
- Pricing: marginal ladder retained for transparency, but contracted blended effective target = $1.95 per 1K tokens (monthly billing, reconciled quarterly). The marginal ladder (for clarity) would be: 0–750M: $2.40, 750M–2.1B: $1.90, 2.1B+: $1.40 per 1K.
- Protection: 250M micro‑tranches for smoothing; 30‑day velocity credit for launch windows (applies up to two occurrences per year).
- Finance: quarterly prepay with a 30‑day settlement window post quarter for true‑up. If Sentinel wants to lock to $1.80 blended, we need an 18‑month term + 25% upfront prepayment or a minimum annual spend guarantee.
- Security: SOC2 report attached; we’ll add a security contact in the appendix and a 30‑day evidence SLA.

If that looks acceptable I can route for signature — DocuSign: https://docusign.com/XYZ-Redwood-Sentinel — or send a redline version of the PDF if you prefer to mark changes.

Look forward to your feedback,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
